instruments.counterparty: Enron Capital and Trade Resources Corp.
instruments.notes: Enron Hedge: cost free collar on NYMEX Light Sweet Crude Oil Futures average monthly price; monthly amounts escalate from 8,500 Bbls in Jan 1996 to 14,000 Bbls in Dec 2000 (volume_total not stated).
instruments.evidence_quote:
hedges crude oil production over a five year period beginning January 1, 1996 in monthly amounts
escalating from 8,500 Bbls in January 1996 to 14,000 Bbls in December 2000.

instruments.notes: Contract entered Jan 1, 1997 for a $34,170 payment that exactly offsets the effect of the Enron Hedge during Jan 1998 through Dec 2000; price terms and volumes not stated separately.
instruments.evidence_quote:
On January 1, 1997, the Company paid $34,170 to enter into a
contract with Koch Gas Services Company ("Koch") that exactly offsets the effect
of the Enron Hedge during the period January 1998 through December 2000.

instruments.notes: 100,000 barrels per month; Company paid $33,000 for this contract, amortized over the contract period.
instruments.evidence_quote:
The Company has also entered into a put
contract with Enron for 100,000 barrels per month from January 1998 through
March 1998 at a put price of $16.00 per barrel.

instruments.notes: Cost free collar entered March 12, 1998 (subsequent event), based on NYMEX Light Sweet Crude Oil Futures; 75,000 barrels per month.
instruments.evidence_quote:
On March 12, 1998, the Company entered into a cost free collar with Enron
whereby the average monthly price, based on NYMEX Light Sweet Crude Oil Futures
Contracts, is between $14.50 and $17.70 per barrel.

hedging_summary.stated_hedging_policy: Periodically enters into commodity contracts to hedge or reduce impact of oil and gas price fluctuations and to help ensure repayment of indebtedness; costs and settlements adjust revenue when sold.
